answer.rationale: The 18% cost cut and the 14-day expiry of the primary contract (no auto-renew) force action now; memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal preserved integration stability and deliveries, memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor cut unit cost but that alone may not achieve 18% or preserve delivery certainty, and memory_c4 shows renegotiation at renewal recovered margin and moved price/payment terms. Since only one decision is permitted this cycle, adding a second source or switching primary outright would increase delivery risk at 94% line utilization with no buffer; deferring risks contract lapse and line stoppage. Negotiating renewal terms with the incumbent lets us target the 18% reduction through price concessions, payment terms, and possibly volume/multi-year leverage (per memory_c6) while preserving the existing integration and delivery schedule. Verifying memory_c2 before committing confirms the low-cost vendor's actual cost advantage and reliability, preserving it as a credible fallback/leverage in the negotiation.
